---
title: Submit to the Showcase
description: Add your migrated blog to the medmark showcase with a pull request.
---

The [showcase](/showcase) lists blogs and sites whose content was migrated off Medium with medmark. If you've moved your
own writing across, please add it — it helps other people see what the output looks like in the wild.

Adding an entry is a change to a single JSON file. No build step, no code.

## What qualifies

- The site is **publicly reachable** over HTTPS.
- At least some of its content was **converted with medmark**.
- It isn't primarily an ad, a paywall, or a link farm.

That's the whole bar. Personal blogs with three posts are as welcome as company engineering sites.

## The quick way

<Steps>

<Step>

### Open the file on GitHub

Use GitHub's web editor — it forks the repository and creates the branch for you:

[Edit `showcase.json` →](https://github.com/brionmario/medmark/edit/main/apps/website/content/showcase.json)

</Step>

<Step>

### Add your entry

Append an object to the `sites` array:

```json title="apps/website/content/showcase.json"
{
  "sites": [
    {
      "name": "Your Blog",
      "url": "https://example.com/blog",
      "description": "One sentence about what you write about.",
      "author": {
        "name": "Your Name",
        "github": "your-github-username"
      },
      "repo": "https://github.com/your-github-username/your-site",
      "tags": ["Next.js", "MDX"]
    }
  ]
}
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Open the pull request

Use the **showcase** pull request template so the checks are obvious to whoever reviews it:

[Open a showcase PR →](https://github.com/brionmario/medmark/compare?template=showcase.md)

</Step>

</Steps>

## The local way

If you'd rather run it locally:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/brionmario/medmark.git
cd medmark
pnpm install

# edit apps/website/content/showcase.json

pnpm --filter @medmark/website dev
```

Then open [localhost:3000/showcase](http://localhost:3000/showcase) to see your card before you push.

## Entry fields

| Field           | Required | Description                                                     |
| --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | yes      | The site or blog name, as it should be displayed (max 60 chars) |
| `url`           | yes      | `https://` link to the page built from medmark output           |
| `description`   | yes      | One sentence, max 160 characters                                |
| `author.name`   | yes      | Who maintains the site                                          |
| `author.github` | no       | GitHub username, without the `@`                                |
| `repo`          | no       | `https://` link to the site's source repository                 |
| `tags`          | no       | Up to 6 short labels, e.g. the framework used                   |

The file has a JSON Schema next to it (`showcase.schema.json`), so an editor with schema support will flag a typo before
you commit.

## House rules

- **Keep the array sorted by `name`.** The page sorts entries itself, but a sorted file keeps diffs small.
- **One site per pull request.** It keeps review simple, and a problem with one entry doesn't hold up another.
- **Link the page, not the homepage** — if your posts live at `/blog`, link `/blog`.
- **Describe, don't advertise.** "Notes on distributed systems" reads better than "The #1 resource for engineers".

## What happens next

A maintainer checks that the link resolves and that the entry parses, then merges. The showcase page is statically
generated, so your card appears the next time the site is deployed.

<Callout title="Something wrong with an existing entry?">
  Links rot and people move on. Open a pull request removing or updating the entry — no need to ask first if it's your
  own.
</Callout>
